title: 2025-07-22-roadmap-launch-readiness-internal-sync

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex, Sana, Marcus, Priya, Evan, Dina
Links shared: slides - internal link (drive/redwood/serve-v2); benchmark doc - drive/redwood/benchmarks/2025-07; postmortem - drive/redwood/postmortems/2025-07-15-tail-latency

[00:00] Alex: alright, uh thanks everyone for joining on time. I'll kick us off, this is the roadmap and launch readiness sync for Serve v2 and Optimize. We also want a quick run through the incident from last week. Sana, do you want to start with status on the rollout?

[00:18] Sana: yeah sure, so the build is green, performance tests mostly pass, there's one flaky E2E around the kv cache warmup that Dina is looking at, um. Canary image is pushed to staging cluster, config is in the canary branch, but we need to lock the autoscaler thresholds. Right now our default is 60s scale up which is maybe too slow for some tail loads.

[00:46] Marcus: hm yeah that 60s is probably too conservative, we saw the tail latency spike during the 15th incident when burst traffic hit the gpu pool and cold kv cache increased p99s to like 1.2 seconds. Which is bad for low-latency customers.

[01:05] Dina: yeah the regression seems tied to kv cache eviction behavior when sequence lengths are higher than expected. Some of the testing queries didn't mimic our real traffic, sorry about that.

[01:22] Priya: quick question — are we sure it's eviction and not the kernel selection fallback? we have two failure modes: cache misses that fetch large KV blobs, or the runtime switching to slower kernels for long sequences. We should confirm which one dominated.

[01:40] Evan: I instrumented the runtime logs; the metrics show both. On the 15th we had a small burst that caused a cascade: cache misses increased, which increased memory pressure, kernel planner fell back to fallback kernels on some nodes, and that increased compute time. So it's a combo.

[02:05] Alex: ok that's actually helpful. For launch readiness we should have mitigations for both. What's the short-term fix vs long-term?

[02:18] Sana: short-term I propose tightening autoscaler thresholds and enabling a small pre-warm pool for bursty routes, plus a temporary KV cache size bump for canary. Long-term we need better kernel planner heuristics and prefetching for KV entries.

[02:37] Marcus: agree. I'll own the autoscaler tuning and pre-warm pool as SRE, and Evan can own the cache bump and monitor costs. We'll measure cost delta in the Optimize dashboard.

[02:52] Priya: what's the customer impact window if we do the cache size bump? we need to signal to sales and CSMs.

[03:00] Alex: good point. Priya, you'll draft a short customer note — when we do canary we'll include the rollback plan and a pointer to the support runbook.

[03:14] Dina: on the QA front, I'll run regression with realistic seq length distribution and pay particular attention to warmup behavior. I think our synthetic tests used shorter sequences, which missed the failure mode.

[03:32] Sana: also worth calling out the cloud region behaviour — the incident had disproportionate effect in eu-west-2 because capacity was saturated there. We should consider regional canarying as well.

[03:48] Marcus: yes regional routing rules will be part of canary plan. We'll route a small percentage in each major region first.

[04:00] Alex: moving on to Optimize features — batching recommendations, quant profiles. Where are we on docs and QA for Optimize?

[04:12] Evan: optimize's quantization profiles are ready for internal testing. We have model-level profiles for 8-bit and some 4-bit heuristics. The main risk is quality regression for certain prompts. We need a prompt-set based eval run against customer workloads.

[04:34] Priya: we already have an eval harness but it's not broad enough. I'll get the growth team to share representative prompts, and we should run A/B evals on canary traffic.

[04:50] Sana: timeline wise, we should not enable aggressive quant on host routes until we have auto-rollback on quality regression triggered by eval thresholds. That feature isn't in yet. For launch, default is conservative quant and recommendations flag for customers.

[05:10] Marcus: ops-wise we need to ensure cost dashboards reflect quant impact per-route and expose it in the Console. If customers enable recommendations we want to show projected dollar savings and estimated latency changes.

[05:28] Alex: can someone own a short checklist for Console updates? we need dashboard card, docs blurb, and alerting if quant leads to >2% quality drop.

[05:40] Evan: I'll do the dashboard card. Alex you take docs?

[05:45] Alex: yeah I'll coordinate with docs but Priya will lead the customer-facing launch notes.

[05:52] Dina: quick note on the incident postmortem — I updated the draft postmortem in drive. The RCA currently lists three contributing factors: cache eviction, kernel fallback, and regional capacity constraint. Comments welcome.

[06:10] Priya: I left comments, suggest we add a short customer-facing blurb for transparency. Also we should indicate our mitigation timeline.

[06:24] Marcus: operationally, I'd like a runbook tweak: add a step to check kv cache hit-rate heatmap as the first triage, and a playbook for pre-warm pool enable/disable.

[06:38] Sana: agreed. Also for deployment we need a canary window length suggestion — propose 72 hours with automated rollback if p99 increases >15% over baseline for two consecutive hours. Thoughts?

[06:55] Evan: 72 hours seems ok but we should do region-staggered canaries so not all regions hit that window at once. Also make sure canary logs are exported to the centralized trace storage for quick debugging.

[07:10] Alex: good. Let's capture the acceptance criteria for the rollout: 1) tail latency within 10% of baseline on canary, 2) no quality regressions above threshold on eval harness, 3) docs and runbooks updated, 4) rollback validated.

[07:30] Priya: I'll add that to the launch checklist. Also can we confirm who communicates to sales/CSM for customers on dedicated plans? We need to give them heads-up about possible short maintenance windows.

[07:44] Sana: that's Sales Ops territory — Alex and Priya can coordinate and provide the message.

[07:52] Marcus: quick note about monitoring — we should add a synthetic probe that exercises long sequence lengths monthly, and an alert if kv miss-rate climbs above 5%.

[08:06] Dina: I'll add that probe to the QA plan and schedule it.

[08:18] Alex: ok, shifting to timeline: target internal canary start 2025-07-27, expanded canary 2025-07-30, general availability tentatively 2025-08-07 pending results. Any blockers?

[08:32] Sana: blockers: canary config finalization, QA regression completion, and a small change to the kernel planner which is low risk but needs perf signoff.

[08:46] Evan: I'm finishing the cache metrics dashboard today and will share screenshots. That should help Marcus evaluate cost tradeoffs.

[08:56] Priya: Sales enablement content draft will be ready by 2025-07-25, I'll loop in the Solutions folks.

[09:06] Alex: excellent. Back to the incident items — who will finalize the postmortem?

[09:12] Dina: I'll own the postmortem finalization once comments are in, aiming for 2025-07-24.

[09:20] Marcus: and I'll run the extended tail-latency benchmark against staging with realistic traffic tomorrow and upload results.

[09:30] Alex: cool. Any other operational concerns?

[09:36] Sana: one last thing — we should validate compliance docs for Private customers; some enterprise customers asked about audit logs during the incident. We need an FAQ entry about how audit logs show fallback events.

[09:50] Priya: I'll add the FAQ item to the security docs and coordinate with Compliance.

[10:00] Alex: alright let's recap quickly, high level decisions: tighten autoscaler & pre-warm pool for canary (Marcus), KV cache bump & metric heatmaps (Evan), tighten QA and run regression with long sequences (Dina), Priya to lead customer comms and launch checklist, Sana to finalize canary k8s manifests. Canaries region-staggered for 72 hours with rollback criteria spelled out.

[10:25] Alex: next steps are in the notes and action items. I'll follow up with calendar invites for the tabletop and the canary kickoff. Thanks everyone.

[10:35] (meeting ends)
